holidays.name: National Chocolate Cake Day
holidays.description: A day for indulging in rich, fudgy chocolate cake in all its forms, from towering layer cakes to molten lava cups. Bakeries and home cooks celebrate with extra frosting and no regrets.
holidays.origin: An unofficial American food holiday, popularized by food-calendar websites and social media celebrations. It has no single known founder or official proclamation.
holidays.funFact: Chocolate was consumed as a bitter drink for centuries. Chocolate cake as we know it did not emerge until the 1800s, after advances in processing made cocoa powder widely available.

holidays.name: International Holocaust Remembrance Day
holidays.description: A solemn day honoring the victims of the Holocaust through education, memorials, and reflection. It is observed worldwide with ceremonies, museum programs, and educational events.
holidays.origin: The United Nations General Assembly designated the day in 2005. January 27 marks the 1945 liberation of the Auschwitz-Birkenau camp by Soviet troops.
holidays.funFact: Although this is a serious observance rather than a quirky one, it is one of the few days recognized by the UN that is marked in nearly every country, with landmarks around the world lit up in remembrance.

holidays.name: Thomas Crapper Day
holidays.description: A day to celebrate the legendary plumber associated with the flush toilet. People celebrate with bathroom humor, plumbing appreciation, and toasts to modern sanitation.
holidays.origin: Observed in honor of Thomas Crapper, an English plumber and businessman, whose death is commemorated around this date. He ran a sanitary ware company in Victorian London.
holidays.funFact: Crapper did not invent the flush toilet, despite the popular myth. He did hold several patents related to plumbing improvements, and his name was prominently displayed on his products.

holidays.name: Punch the Clock Day
holidays.description: A tongue-in-cheek workplace observance recognizing the daily grind of showing up on time. It is a day to appreciate your coworkers and maybe chuckle about the time clock.
holidays.origin: An unofficial workplace-themed observance that grew out of online holiday calendars. It plays on the idea of the old mechanical time clock used in factories and offices.
holidays.funFact: The first time clock was invented in 1888 by Willard Bundy, a jeweler in Auburn, New York, to track the hours his workers kept.

holidays.name: Rubber Duckie Day
holidays.description: A bubbly celebration of the beloved yellow bath toy, with floating ducks, bath-time fun, and a nostalgic nod to Sesame Street's famous song.
holidays.origin: Rubber Duckie Day is observed on January 13 in many calendars, but some lists and fan celebrations tie it to late January and the birthday of Lewis Carroll, the author of Alice in Wonderland, on January 27, whose whimsical writing inspires playful celebrations.
holidays.funFact: In 1992, a shipping container carrying about 29,000 plastic bath toys fell overboard in the Pacific Ocean. The toys helped oceanographers track currents and drifted for years, washing ashore across the globe.
